text:
Henry's total trip is 60 miles.  
The first stop is 20 miles from the start.  
The second stop is 15 miles before the end, so it is at 60 - 15 = 45 miles from the start.  
The distance between the first stop and the second stop is 45 - 20 = 25 miles.

Answer: 25
reasoning:
We are given: "Henry made two stops during his 60-mile bike trip. He first stopped after 20 miles. His second stop was 15 miles before the end of the trip. How many miles did he travel between his first and second stops?"

Total trip = 60 miles.
First stop: after 20 miles. So distance from start to first stop = 20 miles.
Second stop: 15 miles before the end of the trip. So distance from second stop to end = 15 miles. Therefore, distance traveled from start to second stop = 60 - 15 = 45 miles.
Distance traveled between first and second stops = distance from start to second stop minus distance from start to first stop = 45 - 20 = 25 miles.
Answer: 25 miles.
